highlight.title: Next.js 16.2: AI-Ready Development
highlight.summary: <cite index="3-11,3-12">Next.js 16.2 introduces AI-ready create-next-app templates, browser log forwarding for debugging, dev server lock file handling, and experimental Agent DevTools.</cite> <cite index="10-2">Turbopack delivers 400% faster dev server startup with Server Fast Refresh and improved file system caching.</cite>

resources.title: TypeScript 5.7: Path Rewriting & Performance
resources.why_now: <cite index="13-6,13-13">The path rewriting feature for relative imports makes it worth upgrading for modern Node.js projects, while TypeScript can now rewrite relative import paths when compiling.</cite>

resources.title: Full-Stack Architecture Stack Guide for 2026
resources.why_now: <cite index="24-1">This guide was restructured around twelve universal architecture concerns translated from cross-language backend best practices into concrete Next.js mappings.</cite>

resources.title: AI-Native SaaS Architecture Patterns
resources.why_now: <cite index="23-12,23-14">Building AI-native SaaS in 2026 requires different architecture than traditional web apps, handling non-deterministic outputs and per-user AI costs.</cite>

resources.title: React & Next.js Evolution Roadmap 2026
resources.why_now: <cite index="7-27,7-33,7-34">2026 will be about depth rather than new features - if you haven't migrated to React 19, Next.js 16, or Turbopack, this is the year to complete that work.</cite>

claude_take: <cite index="6-12">React 19's compiler, TypeScript 5.7's stricter inference, and Node 22 LTS aren't cosmetic upgrades - they change how your code runs.</cite> The ecosystem is consolidating around mature patterns rather than chasing new frameworks, making this an ideal time to master the fundamentals that will remain relevant long-term.
